prompt: Two numbers MULTIPLY to $12$ and ADD to $7$. What is the larger of the two numbers?
hint: Start with the multiplying condition because only a few whole-number pairs satisfy it. Then test each pair against the sum.

hints.text: Start with the multiplying condition because only a few whole-number pairs satisfy it. Then test each pair against the sum.
The pairs that multiply to $12$ are $1$ and $12$, $2$ and $6$, and $3$ and $4$. Find each sum and look for $7$.
$3 + 4 = 7$, so the numbers are $3$ and $4$, and the larger one is $4$.

explanation: List the whole-number pairs that multiply to $12$: $1$ and $12$, $2$ and $6$, $3$ and $4$.
Check the sum of each pair. Only $3 + 4$ gives $7$, since the others give $13$ and $8$.
The two numbers are $3$ and $4$, so the larger number is $4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why this hunt matters
steps: This is the exact search you use to factor x² + 7x + 12.
The pair 3 and 4 becomes (x + 3)(x + 4) — the number hunt IS factoring practice.

alternativeExplanations.title: Split 7 and test
steps: Multiply each: 6, 10, 12. Only 3 × 4 hits 12, so the numbers are 3 and 4.
